newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela takes aim at drug money laundering.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela takes aim at drug money laundering.

text.p: Venezuela unveiled Tuesday new banking rules to clamp down on the laundering of drug money which officials said could run to $4 billion per year.
Under the new regulations, banks and other financial institutions must inform authorities of any suspicious transactions and provide full details of all movements over $10,000.

"We're next door to Colombia, which is the biggest drugs producer in the world, and this exposes us to being infected by the illnesses of that country," Carlos Tablante, head of the National Anti-Drugs Commission (CNA), told reporters.
Banks found to be involved in money laundering could be closed down and those responsible jailed for up to 20 years.
Although no official figures exist, the CNA has estimated that money laundering in Venezuela could account for up to five percent of the country's gross domestic product, or $4 billion.

"We are aware that there is a great problem hanging over us to which we have to be alert and draw up our own plans," said Tablante who also called for a separate bill to regulate political campaign financing ahead of Dec 1998 elections.
